quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: To reduce the chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Riding next to another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you talk to the other rider.
Makes it easier for other cars to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. Doing this limits the escape routes for both of you if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe if you use only the front brake.
Safe if you use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is not as easy as braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make things worse by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear clothing that is bright orange, red, yellow, or green.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that are high enough to support and cover your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and not use it again.
Release the front brake and quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake immediately and completely. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: Which of these protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not protect your eyes well enough.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
You stop before you expect to.
It takes too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, your wheels may lose grip on the road and you could crash.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana affects you within minutes and lasts two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used in curves.
It should use the shoulder in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: If a rider wants to go faster than the group, what should happen?

options.text: Let them go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
Speed up to keep up with them.
Split up so everyone rides at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Roll off the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Apply them firmly and do not panic if they lock.

questions.question: What should you do when you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle leans to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When you cannot avoid an obstacle, go straight at it if possible. Slow down. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The other driver will definitely yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will properly yield to you.

questions.question: What is the best formation for group riding to stay close while keeping a safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving everyone enough space to stay safe. Use single-file when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When picking a helmet, which is NOT important?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: It looks good.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.
